plan.question: Compare approaches to short-term and long-term memory in customer-support AI agents, including retrieval, privacy and retention.

alternatives.name: Session-only memory
defining_features: Uses the current conversation or session context without persistent cross-session memory
Limits stored personal data and avoids long-term retrieval
Cannot recall prior interactions after the session unless supplied again

alternatives.name: Persistent conversation-log retrieval
defining_features: Stores conversation turns or transcripts across sessions
Retrieves relevant past exchanges using search or embeddings
Can preserve detailed interaction history but requires controls for sensitive records

alternatives.name: Summarized customer-profile memory
defining_features: Stores selected facts, preferences, and ongoing issues rather than full transcripts
Retrieves compact customer context across sessions
Requires processes to update, correct, and expire derived information

alternatives.name: Hybrid layered memory
defining_features: Combines current-session context with persistent summaries or profiles
May retrieve selected past episodes as well as stable customer facts
Can apply different access, retention, and deletion rules to different memory layers

criteria.description: How well the approach retrieves relevant, accurate context from the current interaction and, where applicable, prior sessions to support customer service.

anchors.poor: Cannot reliably surface useful context for the user's short-term and long-term support needs.
anchors.plausible: Supports useful context within its memory scope, but has notable limits in cross-session recall, relevance, or freshness.
anchors.strong: Reliably surfaces relevant, current context across the short- and long-term memory needs the approach is designed to address.

criteria.description: How well the approach minimizes unnecessary customer data exposure and supports privacy safeguards around stored or retrieved memories.

anchors.poor: Retains or exposes substantial customer information without clear limits on what is stored or retrieved.
anchors.plausible: Offers some data minimization or access controls, but privacy protections are incomplete or difficult to apply consistently.
anchors.strong: Supports data minimization and clear, enforceable controls over what customer information is stored and made available to the agent.

criteria.description: How well the approach supports defined retention periods and reliable correction, expiration, and deletion of customer memories.

anchors.poor: Retention is difficult to limit, and correcting or deleting stored memories is unreliable.
anchors.plausible: Some retention and deletion controls are available, but lifecycle management may be manual or incomplete.
anchors.strong: Retention can be defined for relevant memory types, with dependable correction, expiration, and deletion processes.

assumptions: The comparison is about general memory architectures for customer-support AI agents, not specific vendors or products.
No jurisdiction, regulatory regime, data sensitivity level, or retention period was specified.
No deployment model, technical stack, or customer-support channel was specified.
The requested comparison should cover both within-session context and cross-session memory where an approach supports it.
No stated priority for retrieval_effectiveness, privacy_protection, retention_and_deletion_control: equal default weight 3.
